learningObjective: Distinguish the KV cache read/write pattern in prefill vs decode and characterize the resulting HBM traffic per token.

canonicalClaims.claim: In decode, each step writes exactly one KV entry (O(H_kv * d)) and reads the entire current KV cache (of length P + t). Summed over T steps this gives Θ(T * (P + T) * H_kv * d) read traffic.
conditions: KV cache entries are written once and not overwritten in normal operation.
nonImplications: Does not depend on paged vs contiguous layout; only the total bytes read.
Does not include weight-matrix reads (separate stream).

misconceptions.claim: KV cache entries are rewritten every step to keep them fresh.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Each cache entry is written exactly once when its token is processed.

misconceptions.claim: Decode re-reads previous Q vectors from HBM, not KV.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Q is recomputed each step from the current token's hidden state; KV is the cached quantity.

misconceptions.claim: Prefill never reads KV cache because everything is done in one call.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Attention within prefill still reads KV of earlier positions; a FlashAttention-style kernel streams the reads on-chip but they still exist logically.

implementationFacts: Decode KV cache reads grow linearly with sequence length, which is why long-context decode becomes memory-bandwidth bound on KV.
MQA/GQA reduce H_kv, cutting the constant factor of KV read traffic per token.
performanceScenarios: At long context, KV read bandwidth per step can dominate weight-matrix reads; this motivates KV cache quantization.
